sentences.text:
This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short "MV Act") has been filed by the appellant/insurance company aggrieved by the award dated 19.04.2018 passed in MACT Case No. Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1743 67/2016 by the learned Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katghora (CG).
2.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katghora
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By the impugned award, partly allowing the application filed by the respondents No. 1 to 3/claimants under Section 166 of the MV Act, the learned Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs. 36,64,536/- in their favor.

3. The pleadings of the claim application reflects that the deceased Sukhpal Singh sustained grievous injuries on account of the accident that occurred on 13.06.2015 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle truck bearing registration No. CG10 C3473 driven by respondent No.4 owned by respondent No.5 and Insured with the appellant/Insurance company.
The deceased Sukhpal Singh was taken to NC Hospital Gevra and then to New Korba Hospital where he died during treatment.

4. As per pleadings at the time of accident, the deceased was aged about 40 years and working as a driver in the Sainik Mining and Alias Service, Old V.T. Centre, Gevra and was earning Rs. 24,314/-
per month total compensation of Rs. 46,50,000/- was claimed.

The claim application was resisted by the respondent No.5/owner and denied the averments of the claim application and submit that the driver of the offending vehicle was holding valid and effective driving license the offending vehicle was insured with the appellant/Insurance Company at the time of accident and the liability to pay compensation is upon it.

5. The appellant/Insurance company also filed its statement and submits that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license there is a violation of insurance policy and the deceased also contributed in causing the accident therefore the claim application against it may be dismissed.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1743 6.
On the basis of above broad pleadings, the learned Tribunal framed issues and decided the same in favour of the respondent No.1 to 3/claimants and against the appellant/Insurance Company.

7. Shri B.N.Nande, learned counsel for the appellant submits that thought he Insurance Company is not challenging the monthly income of the deceased to Rs. 24,310/-but the learned Tribunal has committed an error in holding age of the deceased to 45 years on the basis of postmortem report and The New India Insurance Copmany Limited vs Smt. Ratanjit Kour on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88535586/
2 therefore the assessment of compensation is wrong; and the amount of compensation deserves to be reduced as the deceased on the date of accident was aged about 55 years which is also reflected from the driving license of the deceased which was filed by the respondent No.1 to 3/claimants themselves.

sentences.text: He further submits that though the license was not exhibited but since it has been filed by the claimants there was a document available on record for the learned Tribunal to come to a right conclusion with regard to the age of the deceased.

He further submits that from the evidence on record it is established that there was head on collusion between two vehicles and both the vehicles were trucks and in the light of the above, the deceased also contributed to the accident and therefore some portion of amount may be reduced.
He further submits that 30% future prospects is also added which is also on the higher side.
8. Shri Gupta supports the award and submits that just compensation has been awarded and the insurance company has not lead any evidence with regard to contributory negligence.
The Tribunal after having considered the material on record came to a categorical finding that it is the driver of the offending vehicle which was responsible for causing the accident.
However he fairly submits that the photo copy of the driving license of the deceased was filed by the claimants in which the date of birth is mentioned as 25.07.1959.
He further submits that the Courts and Tribunals are required to Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1743 assess just compensation.
He further submits that this court may reassess the compensation and pass an order awarding just compensation to the respondents No.1 to 3/claimants.
9. The first contention which this Court would like to deal is with regard to contributory negligence.
Though there is a collusion between two trucks but the Insurance company has not lead any evidence to substantiate its pleadings.
Apart from the statement of the witnesses and the criminal papers exhibited, the negligence on the part of deceased is proved.
The learned Tribunal has also considered this aspect of the matter and gave a categorical finding that the deceased did not contribute to the accident.
In the opinion of this Court, this finding appears to be just proper and does not require any interference hence it is rejected.
Now the question comes before this Court is with regard to what is the age of the deceased.

In the light of the submission made, above, as the driving license of the deceased was place on record by the claimants themselves, the date of birth of the deceased is 25.07.1959, the accident has occurred on 30.062015, therefore, on the date of accident, the deceased is said to be 55 years of age.

In light of the above and taking guidance from the judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi & others, (2017) 16 SCC 680, Sarla Verma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121 and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and ors., (2018) 18 SCC 130, this Court is inclined to reassess the compensation in the following manner:
10.

Naturally, the income tax is required to be deducted and Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:1743 deducting Rs. 8550/- prevailing at that point of time, yearly income would come The New India Insurance Copmany Limited vs Smt. 3 to Rs. 3,26,922/- and there are three dependents and therefore after deducting 1/3rd from the personal expenses of Rs. 1,08,974/- the yearly dependency would come to Rs.27,948/-.

sentences.text: The deceased was found to be 55 years of age, this Court is inclined to apply the multiplier of 11 and on doing so, the compensation on account of loss of dependency would come to Rs. 23,97,428/-.

Apart from this Rs.70,000/- as loss of estate, funeral expenses and loss of consortium to respondent No.1 and Rs. 80,000/- as Filial and Parental consortium is also added making the total compensation to Rs. 25,47,428/- which this Court holds the respondents No.1 to 3/claimants entitled to receive from the appellant/Insurance Company with 6% form the date of filing of this appeal.
If any amount is deposited by the Insurance Company in terms of the interim order, shall be adjusted.
The appellant/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation assessed by this Court within a period of 60 days.
After deposit, the learned Tribunal shall pass appropriate order with regard to apportionment, investment and disbursement of compensation.
11. The appeal thus allowed with modification of the impugned award as indicated above.
